record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: If S is the spectrum of recurrence-quotient values rho(alpha) for Sturmian slopes alpha, what is the Hausdorff dimension of S or of each interval S ∩ [a, a+1]?

evidence.quote: What is the Hausdorff dimension (see e.g. [31]) of S (or that of each of its intervals S∩ [a, a + 1])?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ be irrational. The Sturmian sequence with slope $\alpha$ is the infinite word $s_\alpha = (s_n)_{n\geq 1} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ defined by $s_n = \lfloor (n+1)\alpha \rfloor - \lfloor n\alpha \rfloor$. For an infinite word $w$, let $R_w(n)$ denote the smallest integer $N$ such that every factor of $w$ of length $n$ occurs in every factor of $w$ of length $N$ (the recurrence function), and define the recurrence quotient
$$\rho(\alpha) := \limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{R_{s_\alpha}(n)}{n}.$$
Let
$$S := \{ \rho(\alpha) : \alpha \in (0,1) \setminus \mathbb{Q} \} \subset \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\}$$
be the spectrum of recurrence-quotient values for Sturmian slopes.

Determine the Hausdorff dimension of $S$, and more generally, for each integer $a \geq 3$, determine the Hausdorff dimension of $S \cap [a, a+1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface work on the structure of the set of values of the recurrence quotient of Sturmian sequences (Cassaigne and others) and related Diophantine/spectral dimension results, but no source directly establishing the Hausdorff dimension of S or of its intervals S ∩ [a, a+1] was found. The status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Limit values of the recurrence quotient of Sturmian sequences
status_evidence.snippet: The recurrence quotient is a real number associated to any symbolic sequence; the article studies the structure of the set of values taken by it for Sturmian sequences.
status_evidence.claim: The set S of recurrence-quotient values for Sturmian sequences has been studied structurally, but no Hausdorff-dimension result is asserted.

status_evidence.title: Exponents of Diophantine approximation in dimension 2 for numbers of Sturmian type
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Diophantine exponents related to Sturmian-type numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Related Diophantine quantities have been analyzed but do not directly compute the Hausdorff dimension of S.
